sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Chavda has demonstrated construction-revenue growth, but cash conversion and funding discipline are not yet consistent with a high-quality compounder. FY26 sales rose 22.6% to ₹320.63 crore while profit fell to ₹17.00 crore; operating cash was negative for a third year. Orders support activity, but supplier advances, WIP and unbilled revenue consume substantial funding. The completed funded model remains conditional on completion costs, collections and financing. This is a research hold, not a purchase recommendation.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Review cutoff: 20 October 2026. NSE Emerge CHAVDA / INE0PT101017 remains an SME trading record; the annual report’s main-board governance requirements arose from a capital threshold, not proof of migration. The ₹52.25 official close is dated 19 October, not live. September’s completed 1:1 bonus gives 65,312,000 shares and the current lot is 2,000. FY21–23 restated and FY24–26 audited standalone histories form the operating baseline. The FY24 annual report confirms listing on 25 September 2023. Financial extraction confidence is medium, forward funding confidence low; all four gates are Conditional rather than a blanket reliability failure.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 4, CASH 2, BAL 4, EXEC 4 and EARN 4 are supported judgments with contrary evidence. BQS is 4.68; raw Growth Quality GQS is 5.80, capped at 5.00 for persistent CASH weakness. D 3, P 4 and L 5 are separately scoreable; R and IAS remain NS because material prospective funding/property inputs remain unresolved. Original weights, coverage and unrenormalized bounds are shown. The conditional base IRR is not substituted for a fully supported R score.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company executes core-and-shell residential, commercial and institutional construction, principally in Gujarat, with owned equipment/formwork and allied construction services. Construction income is ₹320.0235 crore and operating rent ₹0.6079 crore in FY26. Contract profitability depends on labour productivity, procurement, project estimates and customer certification. Revenue recognition based on progress can precede billing or collection; customer advances and retention terms can differ substantially by project. Property investment is a distinct capital-allocation exposure and is not assumed to be interchangeable with the core contracting franchise.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Regional delivery credentials, repeat developer relationships and equipment availability support moderate entry friction. They do not establish pricing power across a competitive contracting market. PSP Projects is a useful larger economic comparator: FY26 standalone revenue ₹2,989.45 crore grew 21.11%, while PAT declined to ₹52.29 crore and core EBITDA margin was 6.0%. PSP’s wider scale, project mix and accounting prevent importing its valuation multiple. Chavda’s much higher reported margin must be assessed together with contract estimates, cash collection and capital employed, not rewarded in isolation. Current Q1 margin compression is contrary evidence to a strong moat.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Comparable standalone revenue for FY21–26 is ₹91.2379/₹109.8224/₹161.8857/₹241.6552/₹261.4243/₹320.6314 crore. Five-year CAGR is about 28.6%, with a roughly 25.6% three-year rate, supporting REV 8. Historical restatement removed GST from both revenue and material cost without a profit effect and corrected gratuity accruals; gross statutory revenue is not spliced into the restated series. FY26 PAT of ₹16.9983 crore is below FY25 ₹21.1021 crore. Revenue growth therefore remains scoreable while earnings and cash quality are assessed separately.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The 26 August award notice updates backlog to ₹846.92 crore, about 2.64 times FY26 sales. The July ₹89.45 crore ADI Shantigram contract and August ₹54.72 crore Weisdom contract are included in that updated book, not added again. Completion extends into 2028, but awards do not guarantee margins or cash. Q1FY27 revenue of about ₹84 crore rose strongly, while EBITDA margin was 13.6% versus 23.7% a year earlier. The presentation’s 135 working-capital days and return ratios relate to FY26, not Q1. Full operating NWC is substantially broader than that KPI, including supplier advances, WIP, unbilled revenue and retention. Growth that requires repeated equity or escalating debt is not equivalent to high-return reinvestment.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The FY26 annual report discloses a November 2024 income-tax search and March 2026 assessment orders. The assessing officer alleged ₹19.8153 crore of unaccounted construction receipts and raised ₹16.9397 crore tax demand. The company paid ₹2.2258 crore, recognised as a prior-year tax adjustment in the audited P&L, and appealed the remaining ₹14.7139 crore, disclosed as contingent without a provision. Management, citing legal advice, disputes the demand and commissioned an independent review for the audit committee. The auditor included an Emphasis of Matter but did not modify the opinion. These are attributed assessment allegations and a pending appeal, not a finding of criminal guilt. The ₹20.1291 crore investment property is constructed on director-owned leasehold land and was not ready for use at March-end. The note describes a 75% undivided beneficial interest in one property with matching income/cost rights, and a beneficial interest in another without a stated percentage. Legal land title is not in the company’s name. These disclosed arrangements require agreement-level recoverability and completion-budget review; they do not by themselves establish diversion. Related-enterprise purchases were ₹30.0397 crore and sales ₹8.2665 crore. A KMP sales credit note of ₹7.6577 crore reverses the prior-year disclosed amount; its economic terms need review rather than an automatic inference of improper sales. Director loans taken and repaid were ₹23.7636/₹23.7472 crore, leaving only about ₹0.0164 crore outstanding. The ₹70,800 inclusive-of-tax fine for a 12-day results delay was paid; this limited procedural event is not the primary governance concern.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY24–26 CFO was negative ₹24.2056/₹42.5660/₹7.7799 crore despite cumulative PAT of ₹56.8596 crore. FY26 cash capex comprises ₹23.8734 crore operating PPE and ₹20.1291 crore investment property, giving FCF negative ₹51.7824 crore. Equity proceeds of ₹91.2 crore supported investment and net debt repayment; they are not operating cash. The ₹10.5834 crore bank/cash caption contains ₹5.645 crore liened deposits, leaving ₹4.9384 crore actual cash, of which ₹3.0983 crore is physical cash. Finance expense ₹18.4284 crore splits into ₹16.2185 crore interest and ₹2.2099 crore other finance cost; this is not an unexplained cash discrepancy. Core EBITDA is ₹57.9975 crore. Removing both prior-year tax charge and release, and tax-effected other income, gives only an illustrative ₹16.8282 crore normalized PAT. Collateral-note March debtors/stock/creditors differ between books and bank statements; bank stock is lower, not higher. Those selected collateral figures do not share an established scope with the full balance sheet, so no unsupported collateral-inflation accusation is made.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At the dated close, equity value is ₹341.26 crore, around 20.1 times reported earnings. Net debt excluding liened deposits is about ₹134.05 crore; this is not a current October balance sheet. Bear/base/bull assumptions are sales growth 5%/15%/25%, EBITDA margin 13%/16%/19%, NWC 90%/77%/70% of sales and terminal EV/EBITDA 6/9/12. The annual model funds old capital creditors, remaining project estimates, maintenance, full NWC and scheduled principal. New draws bear half-year all-in financing cost, solved jointly with tax; ordinary repayments occur at year-end. Conditional bear/base/bull terminal prices ₹2.14/₹92.91/₹283.65 imply annual returns -47.20%/12.20%/40.26%. Peak debt is ₹306.31/₹322.98/₹379.52 crore, versus ₹138.99 crore opening debt. These requirements are not committed credit. The October CARE BBB−/Stable and A3 reaffirmation covers ₹105.43 crore mixed facilities and does not verify unused headroom. Main terminal values exclude investment-property recovery and restricted deposits; separate recovery and dilution tests are provided. Conditional base entry values for 12%/15%/18% annual hurdles are ₹52.72/₹46.19/₹40.61, before costs; these are model sensitivities, not executable buy levels. The model pays the separately excluded ₹0.6367 crore opening net tax provision once in FY27, in addition to taxes on future profits. This is distinct from the outstanding disputed assessment stress. The opening-claim bridge also pays ₹0.447300 crore of excluded current employee/interest claims once in FY27, and retains ₹1.883600 crore of net noncurrent employee/deposit claims as a terminal equity deduction. It does not force noncurrent claims into immediate repayment. Future operating compensation is cash funded with the opening net deficit held constant; existing taxes, capital creditors and normal WC liabilities are not charged twice. The separately excluded ₹0.0008 crore old dividend is paid as financing cash without adding an entitlement for the dated-price buyer.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Cost overruns or delayed certification can erode margin while WIP and advances remain funded. Supplier advances of ₹83.19 crore, receivables of ₹117.69 crore and unbilled revenue of ₹53.23 crore create distinct collection/execution exposures, not automatically duplicate assets. A tax payment could further reduce liquidity, but the appealed balance is not asserted certain. The severe scenario combines declining revenue, 9% margin, 95% NWC, 16% financing cost, higher completion spending, the outstanding ₹14.7139 crore tax call and a 20% supplier-advance cash loss. It produces peak debt about ₹393.72 crore and zero terminal equity. The tax already paid is not paid twice; collection shocks do not simultaneously receive a cash release or tax benefit. Equity and positive operating EBITDA are real offsets, but not assured refinancing. With all identified opening claims included, severe peak required debt is ₹393.7236 crore and terminal price is ₹0.0000; these are conditional requirements, not committed facilities.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold present equity values are about ₹1,706 crore and ₹3,413 crore. At an illustrative 15 times P/E and 6% sustainable net margin, those values require roughly ₹1,896 crore and ₹3,792 crore annual revenue before dilution, equivalent to about 42.7% and 63.9% five-year sales CAGR from FY26. These rates substantially exceed the base case and require much more working capital, execution capacity and finance. A larger business can still fail to deliver a fivefold per-share return if debt and new shares absorb the gain. The conditional bull case is not proof of either target.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Require a scope-consistent bridge from collateral books to bank statements, supplier-advance ageing and subsequent settlement, certified unbilled revenue, retention release and project-level gross margin. Obtain property agreements, beneficial ownership terms and remaining completion invoices. Track the tax appeal and actual cash consequences without treating management’s favourable legal assessment as an outcome. Verify sanctioned funded/non-funded facilities, utilisation, covenant compliance and refinancing costs. Official 60-session mean/median turnover is ₹90.29/₹33.30 lakh; a ₹5 lakh exit at 5% of the lower value is 3.00 sessions, or 4.37 using the weaker 20-session median. Current lot cost is ₹104,500. ESM I, fewer-than-100-PAN, ended mandatory market making and the exchange’s irregular-SME caution limit confidence despite 60 observed trading sessions. The 19 October indicator file applies to 21 October, not retroactively to the quote date.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Completed deep conditional hold. Comparable growth and dated order wins are genuine positives, but persistent negative operating cash, complex capital allocation and unverified prospective financing preclude a high-conviction compounder classification. Quality factors remain available; R/IAS are NS because funding and recovery inputs materially affect the valuation. No automatic G1 failure, blanket G2 critical hold or proven G3 insolvency is asserted. Reconsider after cash conversion, financing and property rights are better evidenced. No personal allocation or trade instruction is made.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary evidence comprises the final prospectus, FY24 and FY26 annual reports, Q1 presentation, April assessment notice, July/August orders, September bonus allotment and October CARE communication. Original property, collateral and tax layouts were checked before drawing conclusions. The prospectus was read through the web PDF after an incomplete local download; selected historical sections, not the whole document, were reviewed. PSP’s primary annual report provides a bounded operating comparison. Market history uses official rupee turnover and the official indicator legend; pre/post-bonus share lots are distinguished. The linked model has annual funded cash and debt bridges, tax/interest circularity, terminal equity, severe stress and margin, growth, WC, capex, tax, collection, property recovery and dilution sensitivities. Remaining gaps are specific, not represented as verified. Opening claims are reconciled separately: current exclusions settle once, normal operating balances remain in WC, and net noncurrent employee/deposit claims reduce terminal equity without an unsupported immediate-payout assumption.

GOV.reason: Disputed material tax assessment, unexplained collateral-note basis and director-land investment rights warrant caution. Contrary evidence: unmodified audit, disclosed appeal/independent review and transaction terms; allegations are not proved wrongdoing. The small paid filing fine is procedural, not the score driver.

MOAT.reason: Regional execution credentials, owned formwork and repeat developer work support moderate capability. Larger PSP and tender competition constrain pricing power; Q1 margin compression contradicts a strong pricing moat.

REV.reason: Comparable five-year CAGR about 28.6% maps to 8, corroborated by roughly 25.6% three-year growth. Restated net-of-GST history avoids gross-revenue inflation. Latest annual growth 22.6% and backlog support scale, while Q1 margin decline is contrary quality evidence, not grounds to erase revenue history.

DUR.reason: August backlog is about 2.64 times FY26 sales and two dated awards extend execution into 2028. Gujarat/property-cycle concentration, labour capacity and customer funding limit durability; backlog is not guaranteed cash.

CAP.reason: Operating and property cash capex of 44.00 exceeds earnings, while supplier advances and WIP tie up substantial capital. Director-land property rights/completion are not sufficiently resolved for a high score. Growing operating scale and disclosed beneficial rights counter a presumption of wasted assets.

CASH.reason: CFO is negative in each FY24–26 despite positive profits, and FY26 FCF is negative 51.78. Retention, unbilled revenue and advances explain but do not eliminate funding consumption. Earlier positive FY21/FY23 CFO and customer advances are retained as counterevidence.

BAL.reason: Debt 138.99 materially exceeds actual free cash 4.94; all 5.645 of FDs are liened. Equity 220.49 and FY26 net debt repayment are offsets, but conditional growth models require substantial additional borrowing and rated facilities are not headroom.

EXEC.reason: Revenue and order wins demonstrate delivery capability. Profit fell despite growth, Q1 margin compressed and collections remain weak; the paid reporting delay adds a limited procedural concern rather than a disqualifying judgment.

EARN.reason: Reported profit is positive, and both prior-tax items can be transparently bridged. Contract estimates, unbilled balances, persistent negative CFO and tax uncertainty reduce reliability of earnings as distributable cash; unmodified audit is a counterweight.

R.reason: Funded base IRR is 12.20%, but remaining completion cash, property recoverability and committed borrowing headroom materially affect per-share value. A conditional model output is not adopted as a supported expected-return score.

D.reason: Net assets and positive EBITDA offer a buffer, but tied advances, collection exposure and severe refinancing drawdown weaken permanent-loss protection. Tax stress is contingent, not assumed certain.

P.reason: Current orders and execution history support growth possibility; margin compression, financing intensity and unresolved funding prevent assigning high confidence to the base path. No statistical probability is claimed.

L.reason: Actual 60-day turnover maps to raw 7 at 3.00 exit days; 20-day stress is 4.37 days. Two-point conservative adjustment reflects ESM I, fewer-than-100-PAN and ended mandatory market making, with 104500-rupee lots and no live depth. All 60 observed sessions prevent inventing nontrading days; exchange cautions are not evidence of misconduct.

GQS.cap_reason: Persistent negative operating cash FY24–26 with CASH 2.

gates.reason: Disputed tax assessment and director-land rights warrant specific diligence; no proved disqualifying integrity event is inferred from allegations or the small paid procedural fine.
Audited operating history remains usable. Bank collateral-note scope, contract estimates and property rights require reconciliation; these do not automatically invalidate every financial factor.

Full annual models show substantial conditional borrowing needs. Rated bank totals and shareholder borrowing authority are not available cash or committed headroom; inability to finance is not established.
Official dated trades support a conditional L estimate, with ESM I and concentration/market-making cautions. No live spread, depth or guaranteed exit is established.

valuation.formulas: Five annual revenue and margin assumptions drive EBITDA. Scenario financing rates are all-in proxies for interest and finance fees, not quoted bank coupon rates; FY26 finance cost 18.4284 includes interest 16.2185 and other finance costs 2.2099. Depreciation is 4.5% of sales, limited to available net operating fixed assets; tax is 25% of positive EBITDA less depreciation and solved interest. CFO deducts cash interest, tax and the annual change in comprehensive operating NWC. FCF pays maintenance capex at 5% of sales, estimated remaining project/property spending over two years, and opening capital creditors separately in FY27. The excluded opening net income-tax provision of 0.6367 is paid once in FY27, separately from future-profit taxes and the disputed assessment stress. All model capex is conservatively treated as non-revenue-producing until reflected in the assumed sales path. Project depreciation treatment is a proxy, not an asset-life schedule. Debt principal runoff of 12.8989 annually is a simplifying assumption, capped at opening debt; refinancing and cash-floor borrowing are explicitly drawn. Scheduled and surplus-cash repayments occur at year-end; new draws bear half-year interest, jointly solved with tax. No future equity proceeds are assumed. September bonus shares are used throughout and create no cash or value. FY26 equity proceeds of 91.2 are already incorporated in opening balances, never added again. Terminal EV is EBITDA times the scenario multiple; equity deducts debt and adds free cash, with investment property and lien deposits excluded in main cases. Separate property recovery and dilution sensitivities are not asserted fair values. IRR=(terminal price/52.25)^0.2-1. Opening-claim extension: first-year CFO includes the separately settled opening tax and excluded current employee/interest claims. Previously accrued taxes and capital creditors are not paid twice. Old unpaid dividends are financing cash outflows without new buyer entitlement. Net noncurrent employee/deposit claims reduce terminal equity once, while normal WC liabilities remain within the operating cash bridge.
